mil3.2.4:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, does one who is not reborn feel any painful feeling?”
mil3.2.4:1.6: “He feels physical feeling, Great King, but he does not feel mental feeling.”
mil3.2.4:1.7: “How, venerable sir, does he feel physical feeling, and how does he not feel mental feeling?”
mil3.2.4:1.8: “Because there has been no ceasing of whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of physical painful feeling, he feels physical painful feeling; because there has been a ceasing of whatever cause and condition there is for the arising of mental painful feeling, he does not feel mental painful feeling.
mil3.2.4:1.10: ‘He feels one feeling: physical, not mental.’”
mil3.2.4:2.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, why does one who feels painful feeling not attain final extinguishment?”
mil3.2.4:2.2: “A perfected one has no attraction or repulsion, Great King, and the perfected ones, being wise, do not make unripe fruit fall; they wait for it to ripen.
mil3.2.4:2.3: This too was spoken, Great King, by the elder Sāriputta, the general of the Dhamma—
mil3.2.4:6.1: The Question on the Feeling of the Person Who Is Reborn: Fourth.
